Consult Summary:
- A patient presents with approximately 2 months of new-onset anxiety, predominantly around work, with sleep disruption, low mood, anhedonia, daytime fatigue, social withdrawal, and episodic palpitations; plan includes referral to talking therapy, sleep support information, and basic blood tests with follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Anxiety and distress related to leaving the house and going to work; fear and dread surrounding work tasks; sleep disturbance; feeling on edge and tense, with daytime functional impairment.
- Time line and progression:
  - Onset about 2 months ago, coinciding with starting a new job in retail (head office team, new sector; boss described as not nice).
  - Symptoms have worsened over time, affecting sleep and daily life; sleep onset is delayed, with lying awake for hours and frequent awakenings due to heart racing and worry about being late.
  - Sleep duration estimated at 3–4 hours on poor nights; many days feel exhausted; energy and interest in activities decreased.
- Exacerbating/initiating factors:
  - New job stress, perceived workplace difficulties, fear of performance.
  - Public transport (tube) described as stressful; overall life largely focused around work.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Palpitations: irregular fast heartbeat, morning occurrence, lasts minutes to about 10 minutes, sometimes with chest discomfort.
  - Mood: persistent low mood, anhedonia, reduced enjoyment of activities; feelings of being on edge most of the time.
  - Sleep: significant insomnia; non-restorative sleep.
  - Social/occupational impact: avoidance of social activities to an extent; difficulty engaging in hobbies; ongoing work-related stress.
- Systems review and pertinent negatives:
  - No reported suicidal thoughts or plans.
  - No chest pain with exertion; chest discomfort reported only with palpitations.
  - Appetite generally stable; minor increase in chocolate consumption; regular meals.
  - Alcohol: higher intake on Fridays/Saturdays; occasional during the week; quantity not precisely defined.
  - Smoking: occasional.
  - No other medical symptoms noted.
- Additional context from family/social history:
  - Lives with parents.
  - Mother has a history of depression.
  - Open to pursuing help; has discussed with family and is willing to consider therapy.

Past Medical History:
- None documented.
- Medications: none documented.
- Allergies: none documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with two parents.
- Occupation: Works in fashion retailer head office; new job in a stressful environment; limited time for self-care due to work.
- Alcohol: consumption mainly on weekends; not precisely quantified; may exceed typical limits on Fridays/Saturdays.
- Smoking: occasional.
- Illicit drugs: denies use.
- Mental health history: mother with depression; patient uncertain about prior depression, reports this as worse than any prior tension.
- Previous help-seeking: spoke with mother; has not yet pursued formal counseling or therapy.

Family History:
- Mother with depression (past).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- Plan: Basic blood tests to evaluate for potential contributing physical factors to palpitations; results to be reviewed with GP in a follow-up in 1 week after testing.
- If tests are arranged, patient instructed to contact support line to schedule.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Anxiety symptoms with work-related stress, sleep disturbance, and functional impairment.
  - Plan items:
    - Refer for talking therapy via NHS self-referral; provide link to access resources.
    - Provide online resources and sleep-related information to aid coping.
    - No pharmacologic treatment initiated at this time; pharmacotherapy discussed as a possibility if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
    - Advise ongoing self-management strategies and coping resources; follow-up if symptoms escalate or fail to improve.
- Issue 2: Palpitations with accompanying anxiety; likely psychogenic.
  - Plan items:
    - Obtain basic blood tests to rule out organic causes; arrange GP follow-up in about 1 week after results to review.
    - In the meantime, patient to contact support line to organize blood tests.
    - Monitor symptoms; if palpitations worsen or are accompanied by new concerning signs, seek urgent evaluation.
- Issue 3: Depressive symptoms (low mood, anhedonia, reduced interest) coexisting with anxiety.
  - Plan items:
    - Reinforce consideration of talking therapy; provide opportunities for psychological support.
    - Continue to monitor mood; reassess need for increased support or therapy or referral if symptoms persist or worsen.
- General plan:
  - Sleep support information added to notes.
  - Reiterate that medication is not currently recommended as first-line therapy unless indicated by worsening symptoms.
  - Follow-up with GP after blood tests to review results and adjust plan as needed.
  - Encourage use of coping strategies, social connection within safety limits, and engagement in activities as tolerated.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (BP, HR, respiratory rate, temperature) not provided.
  - Full medication reconciliation not provided (no current meds documented beyond none).
  - Allergies not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - No explicit contradictions found in transcript.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversational but coherent; information relevant to psychosocial and somatic symptoms captured; some aspects (e.g., exact alcohol quantities) not quantified in transcript.
